cards.a: Policy-Based Routing forwards traffic based on policy such as source, protocol, or DSCP instead of the routing table. It uses a route-map applied inbound on an interface, giving matching traffic a set action typically a next hop, output interface, or packet marking. PBR is evaluated before the normal longest-match lookup, so it overrides the RIB for matched flows.

cards.q: How does PBR differ from normal routing and BGP policy?
cards.a: IP routing forwards all traffic based on destination plus the RIB; BGP policy affects path selection based on attributes; PBR decides per-flow forwarding based on match criteria. PBR can send traffic to a next hop the RIB would not choose.

cards.q: What is the match-to-set structure of a PBR route-map?
cards.a: route-map PBR permit 10 with match ip address prefix-list VOIP, set ip next-hop 10.1.1.2, and set ip precedence 5. Common match criteria are ip address, ip precedence, and length; forwarding actions are set ip next-hop, set interface, and set default next-hop.

cards.q: What is the difference between set ip next-hop and set default next-hop?
cards.a: set ip next-hop X always sends matched traffic to X when reachable, a strict override; set default next-hop X uses X only if no RIB route exists, a fallback; set interface forces traffic out a given interface.

cards.q: How and where do you apply PBR?
cards.a: Apply route-map PBR inbound on the interface receiving the traffic with ip policy route-map PBR. The next hop must be reachable in the routing table or PBR will not install, and ip local policy route-map applies PBR to locally generated traffic.

show ip policy lists interfaces with their route-maps, show route-map shows match/set statements and counters, and debug ip policy traces PBR decisions. The show route-map counters showing matched traffic are the first verification step.

Sending voice over a dedicated link by matching DSCP EF to a voice-router next hop, steering branch A traffic by source prefix-list to uplink A, marking packets with set ip precedence, and local PBR with ip local policy for the router's own traffic.

cards.q: Which PBR command overrides the routing table?
cards.a: set ip next-hop; it always sends matched traffic to that hop if reachable, whereas set default next-hop only applies when no RIB route exists.

cards.q: What command applies PBR to locally generated traffic?
cards.a: ip local policy route-map PBR. Without it, locally sourced traffic is not affected by interface-applied PBR.

cards.q: When is PBR evaluated relative to the routing table?
cards.a: Before the routing table lookup for matched packets; PBR overrides the RIB for the matched flows.
